title: Translation and validation of the Sleep Apnea Quality of Live Index (SAQLI) for the German-speaking population
summary:
Primary aim of the study is to create a translated and validated version of the sleep apnea quality of live index (SAQLI). First the SAQLI is translated to German by several English-German speaking clinicians. The translated versions are then compared and fused to one translation. This version is translated back to English and compared with the original questionnaire. After eventual adaptations a final German Version is created. This is followed by the validation which is meant ensure that the German version works just as good as the English one. Secondary aim of the study is to validate a visual analog scale for the assessment of a patients live quality with sleep apnea.

For this purpose an experimental group with 100 patients with a confirmed diagnosis of sleep apnea and a control group with about 30 healthy subjects is formed. The experimental group is asked to complete the German version of the SAQLI and several comparable, already validated questionnaires just before and three months after initiation of the therapy with Continuous/Automated Positive Airway Pressure (CPAP/APAP). Those questionnaires are the short form 36 (SF-36), the functional outcome of sleep questionnaire (FOSQ), the Epworth sleepiness scale (ESS) as well as our visual analog scale. The control group is also asked to complete the same questionnaires twice. Prerequisite for the control group is a medical history and basic examination without any signs of sleep apnea as well as a STOP-BANG score of < 3 points.
Last all results undergo statistical analysis and comparison with other studies which translated the SAQLI.

interventions.name:
Experimental group: 
Patients with sleep apnea diagnosed by a polysomnography which complete the SAQLI, the Short form 36 (SF-36), the Functional Outcome of Sleep Questionnaire (FOSQ), the Epworth sleepiness scale (ESS) as well as our visual analog scale just before and three month after initiation

Control: Volunteers without any suspicion for having a sleep-breathing disorder. This group is also asked to complete the same set of questionnaires with an interval of about three month and serves thereby as reference.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Presence of a sleep apnea defined by the criteria of the American Association of Sleep Medicine (AASM) and the Deutschen Gesellschaft für
Schlafmedizin (DGSM)
- Decision for a therapy by the means of an CPAP or APAP
- Sufficient knowledge of German to answer all questionnaires without any comprehension Problem or the need of help
- Age of majority and capacity to consent
Exclusion criteria:
- Disagreement with the study or therapy
- CPAP/APAP usage of less then 300 hours in the first three month (noncompliance)
- Circumstances or recents diagnoses that stand not in connection with sleep apnea and have a strong impact on the live quality e.g. Diagnosis of a cancer or psychiatric disease
